models._description: Purchase Line and Vendor Bill line matching view

behavioral_notes.observation: Confirms an RFQ: validates each line has a product, calls _add_supplier_to_product (auto-registers the vendor in product.supplierinfo, capped at 10 sellers), then either approves directly or routes to a 'to approve' state. If _approval_allowed returns True it calls button_approve which writes state='purchase' and date_approve=now; otherwise state='to approve'. Not visible in metadata.

Approval gating depends on company.po_double_validation: 'one_step' always allows; 'two_step' allows only when amount_total is below po_double_validation_amount (currency-converted); purchase managers (group_purchase_manager) always bypass. This is the configurable PO approval threshold policy, encoded in Python not metadata.

Creates vendor bills: builds account.move records with default_move_type='in_invoice' from order lines (via _prepare_invoice / _prepare_account_move_line), batches/groups by (company, partner, currency), and converts negative-total moves into refunds. This is the PO -> vendor bill (account.move) document side-effect.

Selection: draft(RFQ) -> sent(RFQ Sent) -> 'to approve' -> purchase(Purchase Order) -> done/cancel. button_cancel blocks cancellation if the PO is locked or has non-draft/non-cancel vendor bills, enforcing document-chain integrity.

Read-only SQL view models (analytics & reconciliation): purchase.report for purchase analysis, purchase.bill.union unifies POs and vendor bills, purchase.bill.line.match drives the PO-line/bill-line matching (3-way-match) view. Not stored tables.

information_flows: portal: vendor portal RFQ/PO views and EDI download via /my/rfq and /my/purchase routes

value_streams: Procure-to-Pay: RFQ -> confirmed PO -> receipt -> vendor bill -> reconcile/pay
policies: 8 record rules: multi-company + own/team document visibility scoping
metrics: purchase.report (Purchase Analysis: amounts, delay, qty ordered/received/billed)

classification.rationale: purchase is a procurement support activity feeding the value chain rather than a primary transform. It sources inputs (RFQ -> PO -> vendor bill) so that stock/mrp/sale can operate; its only dependency is account, and its terminal side-effect is a vendor bill (account.move). Maps to APQC 4.2 with activity refs 4.2.4.4 (create/distribute purchase orders, via button_confirm state=purchase) and 4.2.4.6 (reconcile, via vendor bill matching). Classified support per Stabell & Fjeldstad: it provisions inputs for the primary activities.

standard_capabilities: vendor bill creation & PO-to-bill matching (3-way match)
typical_fits: single- or two-step approval by amount threshold
common_gaps: industry-specific approval workflows beyond amount threshold
